body: Where did the previous implementation have issues? Also, I feel like `eaccess` should be used instead.

I had issues where a directory is writable but that function determined it was not writable. That directory is mounted by `sshfs`.
It is easy to switch to `eaccess` or `faccessat` with `AT_EACCESS` flag. Both of them have some unsupported `target_os` or `target_env`.
https://github.com/nix-rust/nix/blob/master/src/fcntl.rs#L26-L38
https://github.com/nix-rust/nix/blob/master/src/unistd.rs#L3418
Why do we need effective ids for this use case?

Wouldn't switching to regular ids be a regression compared to the previous behavior? It was measuring the effective ability to write before. I would rather not keep around the old code, but I feel like `eaccess` should be used on those platforms that support it.
